prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map shows the camera wearer's hands, pen, open notebook, and square tabletop in the bright foreground within arm's reach at roughly 0.3 to 0.7 metres below and in front of the viewpoint, while the floor slopes darker away into the background. Beyond the table at roughly 1.8 to 3.0 metres, a bed extends along the left, an armchair angled toward the left sits in the centre-right next to a small stool about 0.2 metres to its left, and a desk sits behind the stool against the back wall at over 3 metres. In frame 3, a second person enters on the upper right at roughly 2.5 to 3.0 metres away, walking forward and leftward behind the armchair in frame 4 before moving mostly behind the chair and desk in frame 5, with their upper body cropped out of the top of the frame and no face visible toward the camera wearer. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the near tabletop plane from the mid-ground furniture and reveals the continuous floor distance gradient, even where floor tiles and patterned rugs create visual clutter. However, the map is unreliable on thin or flat objects—the pen and notebook pages blend into the tabletop brightness, the walking person in frames 3 to 5 appears as a faint, blurry dark silhouette lacking sharp depth boundaries, and the dark area under the far desk loses geometric detail.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the foreground tabletop (alternately labelled 'bed' or 'dining table') at 0.4 to 0.7 metres directly in front of the camera wearer, an open 'book' resting on its right side within arm's reach, and the camera wearer's hands ('person') overlapping and partially occluding the lower edges of the book and table. In the mid-ground around 1.8 to 3.0 metres away, it segments the 'bed' on the left and the 'chair' in the centre-right (spaced roughly 1.0 metre apart), and in frame 3 it captures the standing 'person' on the upper right about 2.5 metres away and 0.5 metres to the right of the chair before they walk leftward behind the chair in frames 4 and 5. Across the 5 frames, the static furniture masks remain fixed while the camera wearer's right hand mask shifts slightly right to turn a page in frames 3 and 4 and returns left in frame 5, and the background person appears only in frame 3 facing away/leftward with their head cropped above the frame. This map makes object boundaries and category regions—such as the exact footprint of the open notebook and armchair—immediately distinct against patterned surfaces compared to the RGB image. However, it is unreliable in several places: it completely misses the small stool, far desk, and held pen, mislabels the wooden bed leg on the far left as a 'person' in frames 1 to 3, flickers the foreground table's class between 'bed' and 'dining table', drops the camera wearer's hand mask in frame 3, and fails to segment the walking person in frames 4 and 5 when partially occluded behind the chair.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders 3D-like hand skeletons (magenta) for the camera wearer's left and right hands resting on the foreground tabletop and notebook within 0.3 to 0.5 metres in front of and below the viewpoint, spaced roughly 0.15 to 0.25 metres apart. In frames 1 and 5, both the left hand (fingers splayed flat on the left page/table) and the right hand (curled around the pen above the right page) are tracked, showing the right hand slightly higher and to the right of the left hand. Across the sequence, the right hand opens and shifts rightward in frames 3 and 4 to lift the notebook page before returning to a writing posture in frame 5, while the background person walking past at 2.5 to 3.0 metres in frames 3 to 5 has no yellow body or magenta hand skeleton detected at all because their upper torso and head are out of view above the top frame edge. Compared to RGB, the pose map explicitly reveals the fine finger joint articulations and curls of the camera wearer's hands even when the pen or shadows partially obscure the fingers. It is highly unreliable across time, however, completely dropping the right hand skeleton in frame 2, missing the left hand skeleton in frames 3 and 4 despite it remaining clearly visible in the RGB frames, and failing to detect any body keypoints for the camera wearer or the walking background person.
